finding: The dirty-worktree refusal tells the User to "set dispatch.refuse_dirty_feature_worktree: false in docs/testing.yaml" without naming the checkout whose docs/testing.yaml counts. merge-story reads the key from the worktree of the feature branch, and from the primary checkout only when the feature worktree has no docs/testing.yaml. In this repository docs/testing.yaml is tracked, so the feature worktree always has it. A User who edits docs/testing.yaml in the primary checkout, where they usually work, changes nothing and meets the same refusal on the next run. The information is lost in the message text of _refuse_dirty_feature_worktree; the lookup itself is right, and a story branch cannot change the key for its own merge, because the key is read before the merge. The smallest fix is in the same message: name the file as docs/testing.yaml in the worktree it already prints, for example "or set ... false in <worktree>/docs/testing.yaml".
why_this_severity: The refusal stops the merge, names the files and the worktree, and the key works as BR-124 defines (no to fails_purpose). A User who edits the wrong copy of docs/testing.yaml loses one run and has to find out which file dispatch reads. The code exists only on the story branch, so in_use is false.
